finding.claim: The /fetch handler passes the user-supplied `target` query parameter straight to http.Get with no validation. The server fetches any URL an attacker names and returns the response body. That allows access to internal services, cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254), and localhost.
finding.sink: http.Get(target) at main.go:16; the response body is copied back to the client at main.go:22

trace.note: /fetch is registered to the fetch handler and is reachable by any client
target is read from the query string without checks
http.Get(target) issues the outbound request; scheme, host and IP are unrestricted
The response body is returned in full, so this is non-blind SSRF. Error text from err.Error() at line 18 is also returned.

finding.guards_checked: None on this path. There is no allowlist, no scheme check, no private-IP or DNS-rebinding filter, and no redirect restriction. The `allowed` map is used only by safeFetch.

verdict.reason: main.go:15-16 passes the query param `target` unvalidated to http.Get, and main.go:41 registers /fetch with no middleware. The body is returned at main.go:22 and err.Error() at main.go:18, and the `allowed` check at main.go:27 applies only to safeFetch.
